item.title: Briefing - Is Nepal's young leader meeting expectations of change? - 14-09-2026
item.description:
Nepal's leader is the world's youngest serving prime minister. Balendra Shah, who was previously a rapper, was the mayor of the country's capital, Kathmandu, in 2022, before winning the general elections and becoming prime minister in March 2026. After garnering attention with his unusual and social media-oriented communication style, he now has to face the difficult part: leading a landlocked country with a population of 30 million, where one out of five people are classified as poor, and managing the reconstruction of areas devastated by the August 2026 flash floods.

item.title: At a Glance - European Heritage Days 2026 – Heritage at Risk: Revive, Resist, Reimagine - 14-09-2026
item.description:
European Heritage Days have raised awareness of Europe's rich and diverse heritage. Yet, heritage represents much more than the relics of the past: it is a storyteller of our collective memory, and it is up to us to ensure that our cultural legacy remains vibrant and meaningful for generations to come.

item.title: Briefing - Justiciability of Article 2 TEU - 14-09-2026
item.description:
On 21 April 2026, in Commission v Hungary (C-769/22), the Court of Justice of the European Union held for the first time that a manifest and particularly serious breach by a Member State of the fundamental values enshrined in Article 2 of the Treaty on European Union can serve as a self-standing basis for an infringement action against that Member State. The judgment has sparked heated academic debate over the feasibility of the legal standard established by the Court and its implications for future decision-making.

item.title: At a Glance - EU-India trade and investment relations - 11-09-2026
item.description:
In 2025, EU-India trade relations were characterised by a slight decrease in both goods and services, after a steady expansion between 2021 and 2024. In only 4 years, EU imports of goods from India surged by 51 %, reaching €69 billion and breaking the trend of previously similar levels of exports. This resulted in the EU trade deficit growing significantly to €20.7 billion. Following a similar trend, the EU trade deficit in services grew to a new record of €8.6 billion. India became the EU's ninth largest trade partner, with a share of 2.3 % of EU total trade with the world, whereas the EU ranked third on the list of India's main trade partners, with a share of 11.7 %, just behind China and the US (each with a share of 11.9 %).

item.title: At a Glance - Market stability reserve for the EU’s emissions trading system: Ceasing the invalidation of allowances - 11-09-2026
item.description:
The market stability reserve (MSR) is governed by Decision (EU) 2015/1814, which aims to safeguard against substantial fluctuations in market volumes by adjusting the supply of allowances in the carbon market. In the EU emissions trading system (EU ETS), the reserve has been in operation since 2019. The European Commission proposed on 1 April 2026 to amend the MSR in view of ceasing the invalidation of allowances. The proposal seeks to enhance the MSR's capacity to better address future supply shortages or price volatility, while maintaining the EU ETS's market rule-based framework. During its September part-session, the European Parliament is due to debate and vote on its position on the Commission's proposal.

item.description:
The unprecedented crossing of an estimated 80 000 people from Morocco into Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta on 30 July 2026 has highlighted issues with European migration, border-management and crisis-response policies.

item.title: Briefing - New approaches to asylum and integration in the EU: Denmark's migration makeover - 09-09-2026
item.description:
Although originally a country with a liberal approach to migration, Denmark has gradually introduced stricter asylum policies, until returning migrants – rather than integrating them – became the priority. This was in part a reaction to migrants increasing as a share of the population, and the wish to maintain Denmark's generous welfare system.

item.title: At a Glance - Implementation into Union law of measures adopted by regional fisheries management organisations - 09-09-2026
item.description:
The European Union (EU), as a contracting party to several regional fisheries management organisations (RFMOs), is obliged to implement these organisations' decisions into EU law. During the September 2026 plenary session, the European Parliament is due to vote on the agreement resulting from interinstitutional negotiations with the Council of the EU on measures adopted by six RFMOs. The new measures would be implemented through amendments to existing EU legislation.

item.title: Briefing - EU emissions trading system (2026 revision) - 09-09-2026
item.description:
This briefing analyses the impact assessment of the package of three legislative proposals amending the EU Emissions Trading System. The proposals are aligned with the 2040 climate target, aiming to contribute to the EU economy's GHG emissions reduction, including its share of global emissions. The main weakness of this IA is that the information in the IA is disorganised and scattered, and the IA fails to address several important aspects. The IA does not explain the problem nor the objectives of all three proposals. The policy measures are overall explained in detail. The IA analysed the environmental, social and economic impacts of the proposals. A large number of stakeholders were consulted beforehand and their views have been integrated in the IA. Another consultation is currently open until 31 October. Several aspects of the Regulatory Scrutiny Board recommendations have not been addressed properly. The Commission proposals mostly follow the preferred option.

Source : © European Union, 2026 - EP

The European Union, as a contracting party to the General Fisheries Commission for the Mediterranean (GFCM), participates in the management of fisheries in the Mediterranean and the Black Sea, and is obliged to implement GFCM decisions. During the September 2026 plenary session, the European Parliament is due to vote on an agreement with the Council of the EU to incorporate a number of binding GFCM measures into EU law.

item.title: Briefing - Regulating and supervising digital assets: where does control lie? - 08-09-2026
item.description:
The EU has established, through the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCAR), a broad but residual framework for crypto-assets, including specific rules for stablecoin issuers and a harmonised regime for crypto-asset service providers (CASPs). As this framework moves from rule-making to implementation and supervision, a key question is whether regulators and supervisors can identify where control, risk and responsibility actually lie in increasingly complex digital-asset arrangements. Legal classification alone may not provide a full answer: an identifiable issuer may make a legal promise, a public protocol may distribute validation and governance, while exchanges, custodians, wallets and interfaces may concentrate practical control. This briefing examines which characteristics of digital-asset arrangements determine where effective regulation and supervision can act. It develops a layer-based approach covering the instrument, protocol and access layers and applies it to corporate stablecoins and Ethereum. The analysis suggests that policymakers should assess the location of control, transparency, legal and jurisdictional reach, and the practical capacity to reduce risk, rather than treating centralisation or decentralisation as labels for an arrangement as a whole.

Source : © European Union, 2026 - EP

item.title: Study - Beyond declarations: Evaluating CFSP alignment methodologies in Türkiye, the Western Balkans and Accession Trio countries - 08-09-2026
item.description:
Alignment with the European Union’s (EU) Common Foreign and Security Policy has become a central benchmark of enlargement countries’ strategic orientation and a key indicator of the enlargement process’s credibility. Under Chapter 31 and relevant association agreements, candidates are expected to align their foreign, security and defence policies progressively with those of the EU prior to accession. This requirement has gained renewed political importance following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, which has heightened the role of sanctions, geopolitical positioning and foreign policy coherence within enlargement. However, past experience shows that formal pre-accession alignment does not always translate into post-accession cohesion, particularly where candidate countries maintain external dependencies or pursue hedging strategies. Current EU monitoring relies heavily on quantitative indicators, such as declaration alignment rates, which often fail to capture implementation and political intent. This study evaluates the existing methodology (2020–2025) and proposes a revised framework combining quantitative and qualitative indicators to provide a more accurate and policy-relevant assessment of Common Foreign and Security Policy alignment.

Source : © European Union, 2026 - EP

item.title: At a Glance - Draft amending budget No 2/2026: Update on revenue and adjustments to expenditure - 07-09-2026
item.description:
The European Commission's proposed draft amending budget No 2/2026 (DAB 2/2026) to the EU's 2026 general budget seeks to update both the revenue and the expenditure side in the 2026 budget. The Commission aims to increase the level of commitments by €444 million and of payments by €8 billion. The European Parliament is due to vote on the Council's position on DAB 2/2026 during its September plenary session.

item.title: At a Glance - EU-Switzerland PNR Agreement - 07-09-2026
item.description:
The EU and Switzerland have negotiated an agreement enabling the transfer of passenger name record (PNR) data from the EU to Switzerland for the purposes of preventing, detecting, investigating and prosecuting terrorist offences and serious crime. The European Parliament is asked to grant its consent to the conclusion of this agreement. The vote is due to take place during the September 2026 plenary session.

item.title: At a Glance - Omnibus V – Defence readiness - 07-09-2026
item.description:
The Defence Readiness Omnibus package seeks to simplify and adapt EU legislation to strengthen Europe's defence industrial base and accelerate defence preparedness in response to the deteriorating security environment. The package combines legislative and non-legislative measures aimed at reducing administrative burdens, facilitating defence investments and accelerating the development of defence infrastructure. Following a provisional agreement between the Council and the European Parliament in June 2026 on the three legislative files, Parliament is expected to vote on the three texts during its September plenary session.

Source : © European Union, 2026 - EP

item.title: At a Glance - Temporary decarbonisation fund - 07-09-2026
item.description:
On 17 December 2025, the European Commission put forward a proposal to establish a temporary decarbonisation fund. The fund aims to support manufacturers of certain goods with high export levels considered to have an increased risk of carbon leakage following the full implementation of the carbon border adjustment mechanism. Parliament is due to vote on its position during the September 2026 plenary session.

Source : © European Union, 2026 - EP

item.title: At a Glance - Extension of CBAM scope to downstream goods and anti-circumvention measures - 07-09-2026
item.description:
To increase protection against carbon leakage from imported goods containing embedded greenhouse gas emissions, the European Commission proposes to amend the regulation establishing a carbon border adjustment mechanism. The December 2025 proposal aims to extend the regulation to downstream goods and address circumvention. Parliament is due to adopt its position on the file during the September 2026 plenary session.

item.description:
This digest provides a collection of documents prepared by academia, think tanks, other EU institutions and bodies, as well as stakeholders, that can be useful for Members of the European Parliament’s Committee on Budgets to stay informed about the debate concerning the next Multiannual Financial Framework, starting in 2028. The document is produced on a monthly basis by the Budgetary Support Unit of DG BUDG and the European Parliamentary Research Service.

item.title: Briefing - Temporary protection for displaced people from Ukraine extended until March 2028 - 04-09-2026
item.description:
The EU has extended temporary protection for displaced people from Ukraine until 4 March 2028. Because safe return remains impossible due to Russia's ongoing war, a coordinated EU response is still needed. For the first time since March 2022, eligibility has been narrowed: persons who cannot prove that they are authorised by the Ukrainian authorities to leave the country in compliance with their military obligations will no longer be granted temporary protection. At the same time, the EU is preparing an orderly exit from temporary protection once circumstances permit.

Source : © European Union, 2026 - EP

item.title: Briefing - The 2026 State of the Union address: Purpose, historical significance and overview of addresses to the European Parliament since 2010 - 04-09-2026
item.description:
The President of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, is scheduled to deliver her sixth State of the Union address on 16 September 2026. This will be her second address during the current legislative term. She is expected to take stock of the past year and outline the main priorities and initiatives for the forthcoming year.

item.title: Study - The policy priorities of the von der Leyen II Commission: State of play ahead of the 2026 State of the Union address - 04-09-2026
item.description:
This EPRS paper analyses how the European Commission is delivering on the policy agenda set by its President, Ursula von der Leyen, and her College of Commissioners since taking office in December 2024. It provides an initial assessment of the delivery of the agenda's seven priorities on the eve of the 2026 State of the Union address. The von der Leyen II Commission has set seven priorities – different from the six priorities of her first mandate. It has so far announced over 400 initiatives. Almost half of these initiatives fall under the first priority, on prosperity and competitiveness; one in seven under the second, on defence and security; and one in 10 under the third, on social fairness. The remaining initiatives fall under the other four priorities. Two figures provide summary information in infographic format: 1) charting the Commission's legislative and non‑legislative delivery as of 31 August 2026; 2) an overview of progress on all the omnibuses.

Source : © European Union, 2026 - EP
